title: EU Looks to Reduce Cheap Hybrid Cars from China
paragraphs: Two years ago, the European Union (EU) put tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles to protect European carmakers from China's cheap electric cars. Now the EU is having the same problem all over again — this time with hybrid vehicles.

In October 2024, the EU put tariffs of up to 45% on fully electric Chinese cars, saying the Chinese government was offering an unfair amount of help to its country's car companies, which were filling Europe with cheap electric vehicles.
China's electric vehicle sales in the EU fell, at least for a while. But hybrid cars still only had a 10% tariff — and those sales rose.

And while just 3,800 Chinese hybrids were sold in the EU in October 2024, more than 10 times as many — 50,000 — were sold in July this year. A total of 160,000 Chinese hybrids were sold in the EU between January and July.

For now, the EU has asked China to voluntarily reduce its hybrid exports, though it may raise tariffs if China doesn't agree. According to the Financial Times, the hope is that China will limit hybrid exports to about 15% of the EU market, compared to more than one-third today.

According to data from the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association, 2.8 million hybrid cars were sold across the EU between January and August this year — 37% of all vehicles sold. That doesn't include the 760,000 plug-in hybrids sold — another 10% of sales.
As for fully electric vehicles, 1.7 million were sold from January to August, representing 22% of sales.

The EU also wants China to buy more European products. The EU currently spends three times as much buying products from China as China spends on things from the EU — a trade deficit that adds up to more than $1.1 billion a day.
